title: Constructibility of the geometrically irreducible fibre locus
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. The subset
$$E_{\mathrm{irr}}(B/A)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A\mid \operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))\text{ is geometrically irreducible over }\kappa(\mathfrak p)\}$$
is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. The spectrum is [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; geometric irreducibility means irreducibility and nonemptiness after every field extension [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. No flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 055B (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-constructible), level n=1, affine ring form; the geometric fibre is Noetherian since it is of finite type over a field, so having one geometric irreducible component is precisely geometric irreducibility. Local constructibility on the affine base gives constructibility by Properties Tag 054C (lemma-locally-constructible).

proof.text: Choose a presentation $\phi:A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ from the finite-presentation hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-affine-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] to it. This provides the coefficient subring $A_0\subseteq A$, the algebra $B_0$, the finite type morphism $f_0:X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, and the Cartesian square identifying the given family with its base change along $r:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y_0$. In particular $A_0$ is Noetherian. Put $E_0=\{t\in Y_0\mid (X_0)_t\text{ is geometrically irreducible}\}$.

For every nonempty irreducible closed $Z\subseteq Y_0$, apply [lem-trf-geometric-irreducibility-generic-dichotomy] to $f_0$ and $Z$. Its nonempty relatively open $V\subseteq Z$ is either contained in $E_0$ or disjoint from $E_0$. In the disjoint case $E_0\cap Z\subseteq Z\setminus V$, a proper closed subset of $Z$, so $E_0\cap Z$ is not dense in $Z$. [lem-trf-affine-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] gives the one-affine cover of $Y_0$ by the spectrum of the Noetherian ring $A_0$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion] hold, and $E_0$ is constructible.

Use the specified Cartesian identification from step 1 to identify $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}A$. This is an isomorphism over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Pulling it back along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to S$ gives an isomorphism of their fibres over that same residue field, by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-sbc-radicial-preparation-fibre-comparison] with $f=f_0$, $T=Y_0$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the map $r$ from step 1, and $h=\mathrm{id}_{X_0\times_{Y_0}S}$. This $h$ is a universal homeomorphism: all of its base changes are identities by [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. Here $g$ is the projection to $S$. For each $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ the comparison gives $(X_0\times_{Y_0}\operatorname{Spec}A)_{\mathfrak p}$ geometrically irreducible if and only if $(X_0)_{r(\mathfrak p)}$ is geometrically irreducible. [lem-trf-affine-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] identifies that fibre over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Consequently, for every $\mathfrak p$, $\mathfrak p\in E_{\mathrm{irr}}(B/A)$ if and only if $r(\mathfrak p)\in E_0$; thus $E_{\mathrm{irr}}(B/A)=r^{-1}(E_0)$. By [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage] this subset is constructible. The comparison and inverse-image lemma require no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ or $B$.
